## Definition

For $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ and $\eta\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$,
put $Y=X+\eta$. On the domain where $Y$ has full column rank, let
$\operatorname{qf}(Y)$ be the $Q$ factor in the unique reduced QR factorization
$Y=QR$ with $R$ upper triangular and positive diagonal. Define the **QR map**
by $R_X^{\rm QR}(\eta)=\operatorname{qf}(X+\eta)$. Define the **polar map**
by
$$R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2},$$
where the exponent denotes the inverse of the unique positive-definite square
root. For a Grassmann tangent at $[X]$, use its unique horizontal representative
$\eta$ satisfying $X^{\mathsf T}\eta=0$ and define the induced map by taking the
output column space. Under $X\mapsto XQ$, this representative changes to
$\eta Q$, so the input matrix changes to $(X+\eta)Q$. The polar formula is
right-equivariant:
$R_{XQ}^{\rm pol}(\eta Q)=R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)Q$ for every $Q\in\operatorname O(r)$.

These are defined only where the displayed input is full rank. In fact, for a
Stiefel tangent $\eta$, $X+\eta$ always has full column rank, since
$\|(X+\eta)v\|_2^2=\|v\|_2^2+\|\eta v\|_2^2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^r$.

## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $m\ge n\ge1$, have full column rank. Successful scaled Householder QR gives the exactly orthonormal reduced representative $\widehat Q$ and computed triangular $\widehat R$ with
$$A+\Delta_Q=\widehat Q\widehat R,\qquad \|\Delta_Q\|_F\le\beta_Q\|A\|_F,\qquad \beta_Q=(1+\kappa_m)^n-1,$$
where $\kappa_m$ is the proved local-step coefficient. Apply the stored reflectors to $b$ by rounded rank-one updates and let $\widehat y$ be the first $n$ coordinates. Set $\beta_b=\beta_Q$. Alternatively, if an explicitly supplied exactly orthonormal $\widehat Q$ has entries admissible as arithmetic inputs and $\widehat y=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat Q^Tb)$ uses sequential rounded dots, set $\beta_b=\sqrt n\,\gamma_m$. Solve $\widehat R\widehat x=\widehat y$ by successful rounded back substitution. Suppose $mu<1$ and $\gamma_{n+3}<1/8$. There exist $\delta b$ and upper triangular $\Delta R$ with
$$(\widehat R+\Delta R)\widehat x=\widehat Q^T(b+\delta b),\qquad \|\delta b\|_2\le\beta_b\|b\|_2,\qquad \|\Delta R\|_F\le\gamma_{n+3}\|\widehat R\|_F.$$
If $\widehat R+\Delta R$ is nonsingular, $\widehat x$ is the unique least-squares solution for $\widetilde A=\widehat Q(\widehat R+\Delta R)$ and $\widetilde b=b+\delta b$. The relative matrix perturbation is at most $\beta_Q+\gamma_{n+3}(1+\beta_Q)$; the right-hand perturbation is at most $\beta_b$. For fixed $m,n$, both perturbation coefficients are $O(u)$. If additionally $\beta_Q\le19\gamma_{n+3}/(1+\gamma_{n+3})$ and $\beta_b\le20\gamma_{n+3}$, both relative data perturbation bounds are at most $20\gamma_{n+3}$. These two coefficient comparisons are additional checks; they do not follow from $mu<1$ and $\gamma_{n+3}<1/8$ alone. Success and nonsingularity are explicit hypotheses.

## Definition

Let $K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$
be an active KKT matrix, where $A$ has full row rank and $H$ is positive
definite on $\ker A$, and let $b\in\mathbb R^N$. By
[[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]], $K$ is
nonsingular. Also supply a terminating exact-storage routine which, for each requested real entry, either returns that same value with an exact representability certificate in the selected floating-point set or returns `unavailable`. Before QR, invoke this routine on every entry of the intended $K$ and $b$, in increasing row and column order for $K$ and increasing index for $b$. If any call is unavailable or its equality/representability certificate is not verified, return `numerical-failure` without a solve certificate. Otherwise use these unchanged stored values, still denoted $K,b$, for both the solve and residual evaluation. No rounded conversion is performed: every successful residual certificate below concerns the original intended data. Assume $Nu<1$, $\gamma_{N+3}<1/8$, and the successful-operation hypotheses of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].

Set $R^{(0)}=K$. For $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, call [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] on the active column $R^{(k)}_{k:N-1,k}$ and trailing block $R^{(k)}_{k:N-1,k+1:N}$. Set $R^{(k+1)}$ equal to $R^{(k)}$ with the returned active block written into those rows and columns, leaving earlier rows and columns unchanged, and store the returned reflector. If a call fails, return `numerical-failure`. After the loop set $\widehat R=R^{(N)}$. Call the stored reflectors on $b$ in the same order, on the matching active row slices and without column overwrites; call the result $\widehat y$. Solve $\widehat R\widehat z=\widehat y$ by descending substitution, for $i=N-1,\ldots,0$: compute the sequential rounded dot $s_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j=i+1}^{N-1}\widehat R_{ij}\widehat z_j)$, then $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat y_i-s_i)$ and $\widehat z_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/\widehat R_{ii})$, following [[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]]. If reflector application or substitution fails, return `numerical-failure`. The perturbation bounds for these procedures are supplied by [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]].

For a returned stored vector $\widehat z$, compute in the specified order
$\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(K\widehat z)$ and
$\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-b)$. Use
[[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]] with $A=K$,
$x=\widehat z$, and $y=b$ to compute
$$g_N=\frac{1+6u}{1-(N-1)u}-1,\qquad W=g_N\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+\|b\|_2),$$
where the product and subtraction use successful sequential dot products
and $(N-1)u<1$. Let $\kappa_N$ be the local coefficient specified by
[[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]], and set
$$\beta_Q=(1+\kappa_N)^N-1,\qquad \beta_b=\beta_Q,\qquad \beta_K=\beta_Q+\gamma_{N+3}(1+\beta_Q),$$
where $\gamma_j=ju/(1-ju)$ is defined by the operationwise model. The QR
theorem supplies an exactly orthonormal $\widehat Q$, a triangular
$\widehat R$, and perturbations satisfying
$$K+\Delta_Q=\widehat Q\widehat R,\quad (\widehat R+\Delta_R)\widehat z=\widehat Q^T(b+\delta b),$$
with $\|\Delta_Q\|_F\le\beta_Q\|K\|_F$,
$\|\Delta_R\|_F\le\gamma_{N+3}\|\widehat R\|_F$, and
$\|\delta b\|_2\le\beta_b\|b\|_2$. Define
$\Delta_K=\Delta_Q+\widehat Q\Delta_R$. Return
$$\eta=\min\left\{\|\widehat r\|_2+W, \beta_K\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+\beta_b\|b\|_2\right\}$$
using exact norms or certified upward bounds. If residual evaluation or a
certified bound fails, return `numerical-failure`. A successful return
certifies a residual upper bound, not a small residual or an accurate exact
solution by itself.

$$\|D\widehat z-r\|_2\le\eta(D,r,\widehat z)$$
for its actual current $D=A_B$ or $A_B^{\mathsf T}$ and right-hand side. If $z_*=D^{-1}r$ denotes the exact solution, then also $\|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le\|D^{-1}\|_2\eta(D,r,\widehat z)$. $$g=\widehat x^{\mathsf T}r_d+\widehat y^{\mathsf T}r_p,\qquad |g|\le\|\widehat x\|_1\|r_d\|_\infty+\|\widehat y\|_1\|r_p\|_\infty.$$
An admitted exact inverse or $H,q$ basis witness proves the current basis nonsingular; every checked $M_D$ bounds the corresponding $\|D^{-1}\|_\infty$. A transition admitted by either exact rational checks or certified intervals satisfies the exact primal or dual pivot rule in the algorithm, and its replacement basis is nonsingular. Only the exact audit's feasibility, dual-sign and zero-gap checks issue `verified-optimal-for-stored-data`. ## Definition

Input a stored residual $r\in\mathbb R^m$, a stored Jacobian $J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$ (using the convention of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), a factorization mode QR or SVD, an arithmetic mode (exact or computed), and a declared singular-value threshold $\tau\ge0$. If $m<n$, immediately return unsupported-shape without requesting a factorization report; all remaining branches assume $m\ge n$. A computed QR report may also carry a verified full-rank certificate $s>0$ asserting $\|Jv\|_2\ge s\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. The target exact step, when it is returned, is the unique minimizer of $\frac12\|r+Jp\|_2^2$ and hence solves $J^TJp=-J^Tr$; this target is asserted only on a full-column-rank branch. Do not form $J^TJ$ in either solve path.

The threshold $\tau$ is used only by the SVD route. For QR mode the exact and computed routes are disjoint. Exact mode requires a supplied exact reduced factorization $J=QR$ with $Q^TQ=I_n$; only this exact factorization may reach the exact-step branch. Computed mode either consumes the report produced from this input pair $(J,-r)$ or forms it by setting $C=[J\mid-r]$ and, for $k=1,\ldots,n$, applying [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] to rows $k,\ldots,m$ of column $k$ and all trailing columns of $C$, including its last right-hand-side column. Embed each returned active block in those rows, leaving earlier rows and columns unchanged, and propagate the first factorization failure. After a successful computed loop, the report consists of the computed upper-triangular block $\widehat R$, the first $n$ entries $\widehat y$ of the transformed last column, and the ordered stored reflector records (including identity markers). The exact orthogonal representatives of those records define the $Q$ used by the conditional backward-stability result; the rounded outputs themselves are not an exact factorization of $J$ and cannot be supplied to the exact branch. In exact mode, a zero diagonal in $R$ returns rank-deficient; otherwise solve $Rp=Q^T(-r)$ by backward substitution and return exact-step($p$). In computed mode, a zero diagonal returns rank-deficient-candidate. Otherwise initialize storage for $\widehat p_0,\ldots,\widehat p_{n-1}$ with all components unassigned, then for $i=n-1,n-2,\ldots,0$ compute $s_i$ by setting $s_i=0$ and, for $j=i+1,i+2,\ldots,n-1$ in increasing order, updating $s_i\leftarrow\operatorname{fl}(s_i+\operatorname{fl}(\widehat R_{ij}\widehat p_j))$; then compute $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat y_i-s_i)$ and $\widehat p_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/\widehat R_{ii})$. Any first arithmetic or range failure returns linear-solve-failure with its stage and indices. A nonzero computed diagonal without an independently verified full-rank certificate $s>0$ for the input matrix $J$ returns rank-unverified with the computed candidate but no full-rank claim. With that certificate, return computed-candidate($\widehat p$). A nonzero computed diagonal alone is not a full-rank certificate. The computed-QR backward-stability conclusion of [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] is attached only when all of that theorem's successful-execution, arithmetic, and nonsingularity hypotheses are supplied; otherwise no backward-stability conclusion is returned.

For SVD mode, the input includes an exact factorization $J=U\Sigma V^T$, or a computed report with finite stored factors $\widehat U_1\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $\widehat\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\sigma_1,\ldots,\widehat\sigma_n)\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ whose entries are nonnegative, and $\widehat V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, together with certified intervals $[\ell_i,u_i]$ satisfying $0\le\ell_i\le\sigma_i(J)\le u_i$ for each singular value $i=1,\ldots,n$. In the exact case, if any $\sigma_i\le\tau$, return rank-below-threshold and no Gauss-Newton step. If every $\sigma_i>\tau$, return
$$p=-V\,\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\sigma_n^{-1})\,U_1^Tr,$$
where $U_1$ consists of the corresponding $n$ left singular vectors. For a computed report, if any $u_i\le\tau$, return rank-below-threshold; otherwise, if any interval satisfies $\ell_i\le\tau<u_i$, return rank-unverified; if every lower endpoint exceeds $\tau$ but some stored $\widehat\sigma_i=0$, return factorization-failure. In the remaining branch, for $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order initialize $z_i=0$ and, for $j=1,\ldots,m$ in increasing order, set $z_i\leftarrow\operatorname{fl}(z_i+\operatorname{fl}(\widehat U_{ji}r_j))$. After these dots, for $i=1,\ldots,n$ set $w_i=\operatorname{fl}(z_i/\widehat\sigma_i)$. For each $j=1,\ldots,n$ initialize $t_j=0$ and, for $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, set $t_j\leftarrow\operatorname{fl}(t_j+\operatorname{fl}(\widehat V_{ji}w_i))$; set $\widehat p_j=-t_j$ by exact sign change. Any first arithmetic or range failure returns linear-solve-failure with its stage and indices. Otherwise return the finite candidate
$$\widehat p=-\widehat V\,\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\widehat\sigma_n^{-1})\,\widehat U_1^Tr$$
with status computed-candidate and make no accuracy claim beyond the supplied report. The displayed formula names the result of the preceding schedule; it is not a second computation. The certified intervals determine only the threshold branch; no computed-SVD accuracy bound is asserted. A computed SVD routine is not defined here; the SVD branch consumes its report.

If the selected factorization reports failure, return factorization-failure; every status other than exact-step is explicitly not a certified exact full-rank Gauss-Newton step.

## Statement

In binary64 RNE take A=((1,1),(0,2^-27)). Its determinant 2^-27 is nonzero. The exact Gram matrix is A^T A=((1,1),(1,1+2^-54)). The spacing above 1 is 2^-52, so the midpoint is 1+2^-53; 1+2^-54 lies strictly below it and rounds to 1. Thus the formed Gram matrix has equal rows and is singular. Reduced QR works directly on A and avoids forming this rounded Gram matrix; the computed stability statement remains conditional on its own hypotheses.

## Definition

This procedure has two admissible modes. All input values are finite stored floating-point numbers. Audits interpret them as exact dyadic rationals, and rounded operations obey [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].

**LP/QP mode.** Let $n\ge1$, $p\ge0$, $Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive semidefinite, and $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ have full row rank. The supplied data are $A,b,c,Q$ for $\min\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx$ subject to $Ax=b$, $x\ge0$; LP is $Q=0$. The iterate inputs are $x>0$, $s>0$, and free $y$. Also supply $0<\sigma<1$, $0<\eta<1$, finite tolerances $\epsilon_p,\epsilon_d,\epsilon_g\ge0$, and an integer update cap $N\ge0$.

**Symmetric-cone mode.** Let $K$ be a nonempty finite product of nonnegative orthant, Lorentz, or positive-semidefinite cones, let $A$ have full row rank, and use the primal-dual pair of [[def-conic-optimization-primal-dual-models]]. Supply $A,b,c,G,h$, a point $x$ with $s=h-Gx\in\operatorname{int}K$, a dual point $z\in\operatorname{int}K^*$, and free $y$. Equality feasibility $Ax=b$ is checked as a residual, not required of the initial point. Also supply $0<\sigma<1$, $0<\eta<1$, finite tolerances $\epsilon_p,\epsilon_d,\epsilon_g\ge0$, and integer cap $N\ge0$. The positive barrier parameter $\nu$ is the sum of the cone-factor parameters.

The input audit checks all dimensions, exact symmetry of $Q$, and full row rank of $A$ by rational elimination. It checks $Q\succeq0$ by finite exact symmetric Schur elimination: reject a negative diagonal; if a positive diagonal exists, permute it to the first position and recurse on its Schur complement; if every diagonal is zero, accept only when every off-diagonal entry is zero. This test is equivalent by completing the square at each positive pivot; with zero diagonal, a nonzero off-diagonal makes one of the vectors $e_i+e_j$ or $e_i-e_j$ have negative quadratic form. In symmetric-cone mode it also checks that each listed factor has a positive finite dimension, that the data match the declared product spaces, and that $A$ has full row rank. All these checks use exact rational arithmetic on the stored dyadic inputs.

In LP/QP mode form
$$r_d=Qx+c-A^Ty-s,\quad r_p=Ax-b,\quad \mu=x^Ts/n,\quad r_c=Xs-\sigma\mu\mathbf1.$$
In symmetric-cone mode form
$$r_d=A^Ty-G^*z-c,\quad r_p=Ax-b,\quad \mu=\langle s,z\rangle/\nu,\quad r_c=s\circ z-\sigma\mu e.$$
In either mode, $\epsilon_p$ bounds $\|r_p\|_2$, $\epsilon_d$ bounds both $\|r_d\|_2$ and $\|r_c\|$, and $\epsilon_g$ bounds the surrogate complementarity gap $n\mu=x^Ts$ in LP/QP mode or $\nu\mu=\langle s,z\rangle$ in symmetric-cone mode. On product cones use Euclidean norms on orthant and Lorentz factors and Frobenius norms on matrix factors. Norm tests compare exact squared values with squared tolerances. The output is a record containing `status`, the last accepted iterate when one exists, update count, audited residuals, and audited gap; it carries the exact audited gap as an objective-suboptimality bound only for status `certified-gap`. The possible statuses are `invalid-input`, `strict-start-unavailable`, `nonpositive-gap`, `certified-gap`, `residual-candidate`, `singular-system`, `lost-range`, `uncertified-newton-solve`, `boundary-status-unavailable`, and `budget-exhausted`. `invalid-input` has no iterate. A residual candidate is diagnostic, never a certificate.

**Interior audits.** For an orthant factor, require every coordinate to be positive. For a Lorentz factor $(t,u)$, require $t>0$ and $t^2-\|u\|_2^2>0$. For a symmetric matrix factor $Y$, test positive definiteness by exact rational Schur elimination: require $Y_{11}>0$, form $S=Y_{2:n,2:n}-Y_{2:n,1}Y_{1,2:n}/Y_{11}$, and repeat on $S$ until the matrix is empty. Completing the square gives $v^TYv=Y_{11}(v_1+Y_{1,2:n}v_{2:n}/Y_{11})^2+v_{2:n}^TSv_{2:n}$, so this finite test succeeds exactly for $Y\succ0$.

**Instructions.** First reject invalid dimensions, nonfinite data, parameters outside their stated domains, or a negative cap with `invalid-input`. Reject an LP/QP start unless $x,s>0$, or a cone start unless $s,z$ pass the interior audits, with `strict-start-unavailable`; this is not an infeasibility claim. Set the accepted-update count to zero and repeat the following audit and update loop.

Compute the residuals and complementarity gap exactly as rational expressions in the stored inputs; compare exact squared norms with squared tolerances. A nonpositive or nonfinite gap returns `nonpositive-gap`. Return `certified-gap` in LP/QP mode only when $Ax=b$, $x,s\ge0$, $Qx+c-A^Ty-s=0$, and $x^Ts\le\epsilon_g$; in cone mode require $Ax=b$, $s=h-Gx\in K$, $z\in K^*$, $A^Ty-G^*z=c$, and $\langle s,z\rangle\le\epsilon_g$. Otherwise, if $\|r_p\|_2\le\epsilon_p$, $\|r_d\|_2\le\epsilon_d$, $\|r_c\|\le\epsilon_d$, and the surrogate gap is at most $\epsilon_g$, return `residual-candidate`. If the update count equals $N$, return `budget-exhausted`.

Assemble the Newton derivative specified in [[def-barrier-central-path-and-newton-residuals]]. In LP/QP mode solve its displayed block system. In symmetric-cone mode solve
$$A\Delta x=-r_p,\qquad A^T\Delta y-G^*\Delta z=-r_d,\qquad \Delta s=-G\Delta x,\qquad \Delta s\circ z+s\circ\Delta z=-r_c.$$
The exact equations form a square system after eliminating $\Delta s$. Form each system coefficient as an exact dyadic expression in the stored inputs, then round that coefficient once to the nearest normal representable value, preserving exact zeros; any failed conversion returns `lost-range`. Convert the exact rational right-hand side $(-r_d,-r_p,-r_c)$ componentwise by the same nearest-normal rule, preserving exact zeros; a failed conversion also returns `lost-range`. In LP/QP mode, [[lem-primal-dual-lp-qp-newton-matrix-nonsingular]] proves nonsingularity of the exact Newton matrix under the stated rank and strict-start hypotheses; in either mode an exact rank audit detects a singular stored system.

Stored floating-point numbers are treated as exact dyadic rationals (rationals with denominator a power of two) for audits; the unit roundoff $u$ and failure behavior of elementary operations are those of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. For a matrix $M$, $\|M\|_F^2$ is the sum of the squares of its entries. Check exact rank by rational row elimination: scan columns from left to right, find the first nonzero entry at or below the next pivot row, swap it into that row, subtract exact multiples to clear entries below, and count pivots. If fewer pivots than rows are found, return `singular-system`. For a full-rank matrix, use a reduced QR solve: for each active column apply [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] to the column and trailing block, store the reflector, apply the stored reflectors in order to the right-hand side using the same sequential dot, scale, multiply, and subtraction order as that procedure, and solve the resulting upper-triangular system by descending substitution $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(q_i-\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j>i}\widehat R_{ij}\widehat d_j))$, $\widehat d_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/\widehat R_{ii})$. A range exception returns `lost-range`; a zero pivot returns `singular-system`. Let $d$ be the system dimension and $\gamma_{d+3}=(d+3)u/(1-(d+3)u)$. Require $(d+3)u<1$, $\gamma_{d+3}<1/8$, and, for the computed triangular factor $\widehat R$, verify with exact dyadic arithmetic that
$$\gamma_{d+3}^2\|\widehat R\|_F^2\|\widehat R^{-1}\|_F^2<1.$$
If the test fails, return `uncertified-newton-solve`. Otherwise [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] applies: the returned direction solves a nearby system with a nonsingular perturbed factor. Compute exactly and report the direction residual both against the rounded stored Newton system and against the original exact rational Newton equations.

For LP/QP mode set
$$\bar\alpha=\min\left(1,\min_{\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i},\min_{\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i}\right),$$
where an empty minimum is $+\infty$, and use $\alpha=\eta\bar\alpha$. In symmetric-cone mode compute a positive safe fraction $\beta$ for each primal-slack and dual factor, and use $\alpha=\eta$ times the minimum of those bounds. For an orthant factor use the same coordinate ratios. For a Lorentz factor at $(t,u)\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal L$ with direction $(\dot t,v)$, set $q=t^2-\|u\|_2^2$ and $c=|\dot t|+\sum_i|v_i|$; take $\beta=1$ if $c=0$, and otherwise $\beta=\min(1,q/(2tc))$. For a positive-semidefinite factor at $Y\succ0$ with symmetric direction $D$, let $L(M)=\sum_{i,j}|M_{ij}|$, compute $Y^{-1}$ by exact rational elimination, and set $C=L(Y^{-1})L(D)$; take $\beta=1$ if $C=0$ and otherwise $\beta=\min(1,1/C)$. These calculations are finite and use exact rational comparisons; their safety is proved by the fraction-to-boundary theorem on the A page.

Round $\alpha$ downward to a positive normal representable value; if none exists, return `lost-range`. Update each stored coordinate as $\operatorname{fl}(v+\operatorname{fl}(\alpha\Delta v))$ under the operationwise model. Any failed operation returns `lost-range`. Before accepting the candidate update, verify exactly that LP/QP variables $x,s$ remain positive, or that cone variables remain interior and $s=h-Gx$ still holds. If an audit fails, reject the candidate and return `boundary-status-unavailable` with the previous accepted iterate. Otherwise accept it, increment the update count, and return to the audit loop. Every factorization, inverse, rank, and safe-fraction calculation is bounded by finite matrix dimensions, and the outer loop is bounded by $N$. No failure status is an infeasibility conclusion; Phase I is a separate model.

## Definition

Let $X$ be a source frame, $\eta\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, and
$Z\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$. For Stiefel transport let $Y=R_X(\eta)$ be
either the QR or polar endpoint. For Grassmann transport, require $\eta$ to be
the unique horizontal representative at $[X]$, so $X^{\mathsf T}\eta=0$, and choose
$Y=R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)$, the polar endpoint; the positive-diagonal QR frame is
not used for this representative-based quotient transport. Define the
**projected Stiefel transport**
$$\mathcal T_Y^{\rm St}(Z):=Z-Y\operatorname{sym}(Y^{\mathsf T}Z),$$
and, for a horizontal source representative $Z$, define the **projected Grassmann transport representative**
$$\mathcal T_Y^{\rm Gr}(Z):=(I-YY^{\mathsf T})Z.$$

## Definition

$\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, a real Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$, or a
complex Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)$, with each tangent
space regarded as a real inner-product space under the corresponding
Frobenius metric. On a real Stiefel manifold or real Grassmannian choose the
induced map of either the real QR or real polar formula from
[[def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions]]; on a complex Grassmannian choose the
complex polar map from [[def-complex-grassmann-polar-retraction]]. Denote the
chosen map by $R$. Let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ and take an initial point
$x_0\in M$. For this regularity, $\operatorname{grad}f(x)$ denotes the
pointwise metric dual of $df_x$: in any orthonormal real basis $e_i$ of
$T_xM$, it is $\sum_i df_x(e_i)e_i$ (the empty sum is zero). This
convention agrees with [[def-riemannian-gradient-of-a-smooth-function]]
when $f$ is smooth; no infinitely differentiable gradient field is required.

Fix $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $0<\gamma_{\rm dec}<1<\gamma_{\rm inc}$,
$0<\theta_C\le1$, a declared model-operator bound $M_B\ge0$, a maximum
radius $\Delta_{\max}>0$, an initial radius $0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{\max}$,
target $\varepsilon\ge0$, and finite outer cap $N\in\mathbb N_0$. Each
self-adjoint real-linear model operator $B_x$ on the Stiefel tangent or
Grassmann horizontal space must satisfy $\|B_x\|_{\rm op}\le M_B$, where
$$\|B_x\|_{\rm op}:=\sup_{s\ne0}\frac{\|B_xs\|}{\|s\|},$$
with $\|B_x\|_{\rm op}=0$ when the tangent space is $\{0\}$. Supply a
subproblem routine $S$ with a finite operation cap $J_S\in\mathbb N_0$; on
input of the current model $m_k$, radius $\Delta_k$, and tangent or horizontal
space, it terminates within that cap and returns either a vector in that space
or `failure`. No quality guarantee is required because the returned vector is
checked below.

Starting with $x_0$ and $\Delta_0$, process $k=0,\ldots,N$ in order:

1. Set $g_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)$. Return $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$ if
   $g_k=0$, $(x_k,\texttt{target-achieved})$ if $\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon$, and
   $(x_k,\texttt{outer-budget-exhausted})$ if $k=N$.
2. Form the real pullback quadratic model
   $$m_k(s)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,B_{x_k}s\rangle.$$
   With $c_k=\langle g_k,B_{x_k}g_k\rangle$, set
   $$\tau_k=\begin{cases}\Delta_k/\|g_k\|,&c_k\le0,\\ \min\{\|g_k\|^2/c_k,\Delta_k/\|g_k\|\},&c_k>0,\end{cases} \qquad p_C=-\tau_k g_k,$$
   and set $P_C=m_k(0)-m_k(p_C)$.
3. Call $S$ on $(m_k,\Delta_k)$ in the current tangent or horizontal space. If
   it returned a vector $q$ with $\|q\|\le\Delta_k$ and
   $m_k(0)-m_k(q)\ge\theta_C P_C$, set $p_k=q$; otherwise set $p_k=p_C$. If
   $\Delta_k\le\|g_k\|/(2M_B)$, replace the candidate by $p_k=p_C$, interpreting
   that threshold as $+\infty$ when $M_B=0$. Set
   $P_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)$.
4. If $P_k\le0$, return $(x_k,\texttt{model-evaluation-failure})$. Otherwise
   evaluate $y_k=R_{x_k}(p_k)$; if the selected retraction is unavailable,
   return $(x_k,\texttt{model-evaluation-failure})$. If $f(y_k)$ cannot be
   evaluated, return the same status. Otherwise set
   $\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/P_k$.
5. If $\rho_k<\eta_1$, reject and set
   $(x_{k+1},\Delta_{k+1})=(x_k,\gamma_{\rm dec}\Delta_k)$. Otherwise accept
   and set $x_{k+1}=y_k$. If also $\rho_k\ge\eta_2$ and $\|p_k\|=\Delta_k$,
   set $\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\gamma_{\rm inc}\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}\}$; in every
   other accepted case set $\Delta_{k+1}=\Delta_k$.

Return the last accepted point with the corresponding stop status. A failed
finite subproblem call, infeasible candidate, or candidate that misses the
fraction-of-Cauchy test uses $p_C$.

## Definition

Input finite stored binary data for the standard-form LP of [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]], with full-row-rank $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, a candidate ordered basis $B$ of $m$ distinct in-range indices, and a nonnegative integer budget $K$ of basis evaluations. Stored values represent their exact dyadic rationals. Invalid dimensions, nonfinite inputs or repeated/out-of-range basis indices return `invalid-input`. Nonsingularity of $C=A_B$ must be established as part of an admitted basis input; a numerical rank threshold is not such an establishment. A basis whose validity is unavailable returns `basis-validity-inconclusive`.

A caller may request a primal or dual simplex transition after an audit, or only an audit. It may supply a finite sequence of transition records, one for each requested basis replacement, from [[alg-revised-primal-simplex-bland-rule]] or [[alg-revised-dual-simplex-with-finite-budget]]. A transition record has fields `mode` (primal or dual), `basis_before` (the ordered current basis, with its validity witness), `leaving_position` $i$, and `entering_index` $j$; it is checked rather than trusted as already verified. The initial basis and each record's `basis_before` must carry the validity witness described here. After a replacement, its checked nonzero pivot coefficient establishes the new basis; any next transition record must carry its own checked validity witness.

An admitted basis input includes either an exact rational inverse witness $G$ with $CG=GC=I_m$, checked exactly, or a rational matrix $H$ and rational $q$ with $0\le q<1$ and $\|I_m-HC\|_\infty\le q$, also checked exactly. For matrices with at least one row, $\|M\|_\infty=\max_i\sum_j|M_{ij}|$; the empty matrix has norm $0$. For vectors it is the maximum absolute coordinate, with empty value $0$. For $m=0$, the empty inverse witness satisfies the identities. If neither validity certificate is verified, return `basis-validity-inconclusive` before factorization. A numerical rank threshold is never a validity certificate.

With an exact inverse witness, first compare `basis_before` with the current ordered basis exactly. Then check a transition by exact rational arithmetic: compute $x_B=Gb$, $y=G^{\mathsf T}c_B$, $d_k=Ga_k$ for every nonbasic $k$, and $\bar c_k=c_k-a_k^{\mathsf T}y$. A primal record is admissible exactly when $x_B\ge0$, $j$ is the least-index nonbasic column with $\bar c_j<0$, some $d_{rj}>0$, and $i$ minimizes $x_{B_r}/d_{rj}$ over rows with $d_{rj}>0$, with ties resolved by least basic-variable index. A dual record is admissible exactly when every nonbasic $\bar c_k\ge0$, $B_i$ is the least-index basic variable with $x_{B_i}<0$, $d_{ij}<0$, and $j$ minimizes $\bar c_k/(-d_{ik})$ over nonbasic $k$ with $d_{ik}<0$, with ties resolved by least variable index. In either case, the checked nonzero pivot coefficient proves the replacement basis nonsingular.

Certified rational enclosures may instead establish a transition. For each current $D=C$ and $D=C^{\mathsf T}$, provide rational $H_D,q_D,M_D$ with $0\le q_D<1$, $\|I_m-H_DD\|_\infty\le q_D$, and $M_D\ge\|H_D\|_\infty/(1-q_D)$; verify these inequalities exactly. For each solve $Dz=r$, combine its returned candidate $\widehat z$ and a rational upper bound $\eta$ for its Step 3 residual bound to form the coordinate intervals $[\widehat z_\ell-M_D\eta,\widehat z_\ell+M_D\eta]$. For closed rational intervals $I=[a,b]$ and $J=[c,d]$, use $I+J=[a+c,b+d]$, $I-J=[a-d,b-c]$, $IJ=[\min\{ac,ad,bc,bd\},\max\{ac,ad,bc,bd\}]$, and $I/J=I\cdot[\min\{1/c,1/d\},\max\{1/c,1/d\}]$ when $0\notin J$; division is undefined otherwise. Evaluate dot products, reduced costs, and ratio expressions with these exact rational endpoint operations. First compare `basis_before` with the current ordered basis exactly. An interval proves a sign or order only when its endpoints imply that relation. If a ratio comparison is not decided by interval endpoints, return `pivot-inconclusive` unless an exact inverse witness $G$ is supplied for the current basis; with $G$, compute the exact rational ratios and compare them exactly, resolving equality by the least-index rule. Admit the record only when the required signs and comparisons, including all least-index rules, are proved. If a needed sign, ratio comparison, or basis match is not established, return `pivot-inconclusive` with the current basis and its last completed audit, without changing the basis.

For $m\ge1$, use the operationwise arithmetic of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with $0<u<1$, $mu<1$, $(m+3)u<1$, and $\gamma_{m+3}<1/8$. All nonzero exact intermediates must be normal. Norms and certificate expressions below are evaluated exactly or by certified upward bounds; failure to obtain a finite valid bound is a numerical failure. Process the following loop:

1. Maintain an attempt counter $t$, initially $0$. If $t=K$, return `budget-exhausted` with the current basis, the last completed audit if any, and the basis to which that audit belongs. Otherwise set $t\leftarrow t+1$ before starting this basis evaluation. Every budget, numerical-failure, basis-validity-inconclusive, or pivot-inconclusive return includes the current basis and identifies the basis associated with any retained audit; state explicitly when no audit exists.
2. Separately for $D=C=A_B$ and $D=C^{\mathsf T}$, copy the current stored entries into a working matrix $W$. For $k=1,\ldots,m$, set $r=m-k+1$, take the active column $x=W_{k:m,k}$ and trailing block $T=W_{k:m,k+1:m}$, and call [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] once on $(x,T)$. On success, save its reflector data and replace the active block $W_{k:m,k:m}$ by its returned output, which writes the new diagonal entry and exact zeros below it; leave earlier rows and columns unchanged. If $x=0$, save an identity marker and leave the trailing block unchanged. Stop with `numerical-failure` at the first failed call, recording the factorization, column $k$, and failure stage. The final $W$ is the computed upper-triangular factor $\widehat R_D$.

   To apply these stored reflectors to any right-hand side $s$, start with $z=s$ and visit $k=1,\ldots,m$ in that same order. Skip an identity marker. Otherwise, on the active suffix $z_{k:m}$ compute the sequential rounded dot $d=\operatorname{fl}(v_k^{\mathsf T}z_{k:m})$, then $p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau_k v_k)$, $u=\operatorname{fl}(p\,d)$ componentwise, and $z_{k:m}=\operatorname{fl}(z_{k:m}-u)$ componentwise, using the operation order of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] without a column overwrite. Stop at the first failure and record the right-hand side, reflector index, and failure stage. For $Dz=s$, apply this replay to obtain the transformed right-hand side and solve $\widehat R_D\widehat z=z$ by descending substitution: for $i=m,\ldots,1$, sequentially compute $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j=i+1}^m(\widehat R_D)_{ij}\widehat z_j)$, $h_i=\operatorname{fl}(z_i-t_i)$, and $\widehat z_i=\operatorname{fl}(h_i/(\widehat R_D)_{ii})$. A zero diagonal or any failed operation returns `numerical-failure` with the solve and row index. Reuse the $C$ factorization for $\widehat x_B$ and every nonbasic direction $\widehat d_j$; reuse the $C^{\mathsf T}$ factorization for $\widehat y$. Never substitute a rounded dense orthogonal product for the exact orthogonal representative in the proof. After every admitted basis replacement discard both factorizations and recompute; no rank-one factorization-update implementation is claimed.
3. Independently certify each returned solve for its actual current matrix $D=C$ or $C^{\mathsf T}$ and right-hand side $r$. Compute $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(D\widehat z)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-r)$ by the sequential products/subtraction of [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]]. Put
$$g_m=\frac{1+6u}{1-(m-1)u}-1,\qquad W=g_m\|D\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+\|r\|_2).$$
With the local coefficient $\kappa_m$ of [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]], put
$$\beta=(1+\kappa_m)^m-1,\qquad \beta_D=\beta+\gamma_{m+3}(1+\beta),$$
and report the valid upper bound
$$\eta(D,r,\widehat z)=\min\{\|\widehat w\|_2+W,\ \beta_D\|D\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+\beta\|r\|_2\}.$$
A finite concrete certificate option uses exact rational arithmetic on the stored dyadic entries and a rational upper bound for $u$ satisfying all displayed admissibility inequalities. Use $\|v\|_2\le\sum_i|v_i|$ and $\|D\|_F\le\sum_{i,j}|D_{ij}|$ as rational upper bounds for every norm in the two nonnegative expressions. For the local coefficient, substitute $\bar e_m=(1+u)^{m+3}-1$ for $e_m=(1+u)^{m/2+3}-1$ in the source formula: put $\bar d_m=\bar e_m+u(2+\bar e_m)$, $a_m=(1+u)/(1-u)^m-1$, $g_m^{\rm QR}=mu/(1-mu)$, $c_m=2((1+a_m)(1+u)^2(1+g_m^{\rm QR})-1)$, and $\bar\kappa_m=\max\{\bar e_m+8\bar d_m,(1+u)c_m+3u\}$. These are rational upper bounds because $m+3\ge m/2+3$ and all constituent nonnegative formulas increase in their arguments. Then $\bar\beta=(1+\bar\kappa_m)^m-1$ and $\bar\beta_D=\bar\beta+\gamma_{m+3}(1+\bar\beta)$ are rational upper bounds for the QR coefficients. Compute both candidate bounds by finite exact rational sums/products/powers and take their minimum as the returned $\eta$. This implements the certificate without a norm oracle; other finite certified upper-bound procedures are allowed. Any factorization, substitution, dot, subtraction, range or certificate failure returns `numerical-failure`, with its stage and the last completed audit; it returns no certificate for the failed solve.
4. Embed $\widehat x_B$ in $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n$ with zero nonbasic entries, and call [[alg-revised-simplex-residual-audit]] on these actual stored $\widehat x,\widehat y$. Retain its exact $r_p=A\widehat x-b$, $r_d=c-A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y$, objective difference $g$, and audit status together with all solve residual bounds. `basis-solves-residual-certified` means only that the returned bounds certify those linear equations; any requested thresholds must also be checked before declaring them met. `verified-optimal-for-stored-data` is issued only by the exact audit's primal/sign/zero-gap checks. Other completed candidates remain `candidate-only`; small residuals or a failed/ambiguous pivot never certify infeasibility.
5. Return if audit-only mode or the caller has no further transition. Otherwise compare the next record with the current basis and apply the exact or enclosure admission predicate above. A failed or unresolved predicate returns `pivot-inconclusive` or `basis-validity-inconclusive`, retaining the current basis and last completed audit. On admission, replace position $i$ by $j$, discard both factorizations, and continue at Step 1. Exact driver invariants remain those of the existing driver, not consequences of successful floating solves.

For $m=0$, skip QR and substitution: the basis and multiplier are empty, every direction is the empty vector, and their basis-equation residuals and solve bounds $\eta$ are zero. Evaluate the existing exact audit with $\widehat x=0$; no basis replacement is possible. The budget and invalid-input branches remain in force.

## Definition

This algorithm performs one finite-budget LM trial update. Inputs are $x\in U$, a $C^1$ residual function $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ on open $U$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $J=Dr$, the exact values $r(x)$ and $J(x)$, a fixed nonsingular $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, an arithmetic mode (exact or computed), a floor $\lambda_{\min}>0$, current damping $\lambda\ge\lambda_{\min}$, factors $\gamma>1$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, a trust radius $\Delta>0$, and an attempt cap $N\ge1$. In computed mode the input values are finite stored numbers treated as the exact data for this update; only arithmetic performed below is rounded. A computed run may include a certificate that the exact scalar product $J(x)^Tr(x)$ is zero. Put $\phi(x)=\|r(x)\|_2^2/2$ and $m_0(p)=\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2/2$. In exact mode the step is the unique minimizer of
$$\tfrac12\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Dp\|_2^2,$$
which is equivalent to solving
$$(J(x)^TJ(x)+\lambda D^TD)p=-J(x)^Tr(x).$$
In computed mode the returned vector is only a candidate for this same subproblem; no exact minimizer claim is made.


In computed mode use [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Evaluate every dot product by initializing $s=0$ and, for indices in increasing order, computing $u=\operatorname{fl}(a_i b_i)$ followed by $s=\operatorname{fl}(s+u)$. Matrix-vector products and squared norms use this schedule row by row and coordinate by coordinate. Each other scalar arithmetic operation uses $\operatorname{fl}$, with copies and sign changes exact; the first failed operation returns the status assigned to its stage. Function evaluation returns either a finite stored residual vector or failure.

For attempts $j=1,\ldots,N$, do the following with the current damping. After a damping change, construct a new augmented matrix and obtain a report for that actual matrix; do not reuse an earlier damping value's factorization or report.

1. In exact arithmetic, if $J(x)^Tr(x)=0$, return stationary before calling the linear solver. In a computed run, evaluate $J(x)^Tr(x)$ by the stated dot schedule and return stationary before the solve only with the supplied certificate that this exact gradient is zero; if evaluating the product fails, return gradient-evaluation-failure; if the computed product is a rounded zero without that certificate, return gradient-unverified and do not form a ratio. Otherwise perform the augmented construction and linear solve afresh inside this attempt at its current damping: Form $A_\lambda=[J(x);\sqrt\lambda D]$ and $s_\lambda=[r(x);0]$, then call [[alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-safeguard]] in QR mode on $(A_\lambda,s_\lambda)$. Exact mode uses the exact positive square root and requires a supplied exact reduced factorization of $A_\lambda$ for each call; absence of that factorization returns linear-solve-failure. This matrix has full column rank because $D$ is nonsingular and $\lambda>0$. In computed mode, copy the stored $J(x)$ and $r(x)$ into the top blocks, compute $t=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt\lambda)$, then fill the bottom block entries $\operatorname{fl}(tD_{ij})$ in increasing row and column order and fill the appended residual entries with exact zeros. Any first arithmetic or range failure in this construction returns linear-solve-failure with its stage and indices. The call receives a computed QR report for this actual stored $A_\lambda$. A computed-candidate is usable only when that report includes the low-level procedure's independently verified full-rank certificate $s_\lambda>0$ for the actual stored matrix, namely $\|A_\lambda v\|_2\ge s_\lambda\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. Pass this bound as the computed report's certificate field; it is not inferred from a nonzero computed diagonal or from positive definiteness of the ideal exact system alone. A rank-unverified report and every other status besides exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode are unusable and return linear-solve-failure with the report. A computed-candidate remains a candidate and carries no convergence guarantee. If the solver status is not exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode, return linear-solve-failure with its report; in particular, rank-unverified is a failure, not a usable trial.
2. If exact mode returns $p=0$ after the nonzero-gradient check, return linear-solve-failure with the inconsistent exact solve report. If computed mode returns $p=0$, return zero-step-unverified and do not compute a ratio. For every remaining candidate $p$ (the zero candidates have already returned a status), compute $\operatorname{pred}=m_0(0)-m_0(p)$. If this computation fails, return model-evaluation-failure; if $\operatorname{pred}\le0$, return nonpositive-predicted-decrease. In either case do not compute a ratio.
3. If computing $x+p$ or $Dp$ fails in the selected arithmetic, return trial-evaluation-failure. If $x+p\notin U$ or $\|Dp\|_2>\Delta$, reject the trial and compute the damping update $\lambda^+=\gamma\lambda$ in the selected arithmetic. If that update fails, is nonfinite, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report. Otherwise set $\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^+$ and continue.
4. Otherwise evaluate $r(x+p)$ and compute $\operatorname{ared}=\phi(x)-\phi(x+p)$ and $\rho=\operatorname{ared}/\operatorname{pred}$. A failed trial evaluation or nonfinite computed result returns trial-evaluation-failure. If $\rho<\eta_1$, reject and compute $\lambda^+=\gamma\lambda$ in the selected arithmetic. If that damping update fails, is nonfinite, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report. Otherwise set $\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^+$. If this was attempt $N$, return rejection-budget-exhausted; otherwise continue.
5. If $\rho\ge\eta_1$, first determine the next damping. If also $\rho\ge\eta_2$ and $\|Dp\|_2=\Delta$, compute $q=\lambda/\gamma$ in exact mode and $q=\operatorname{fl}(\lambda/\gamma)$ in computed mode. If this division fails, has a nonfinite or nonpositive result, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report, without accepting that trial. Otherwise set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\max\{\lambda_{\min},q\}$. In every other accepted case set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\lambda$. Only after the next damping is available, accept and return $x+p$, $p$, $\rho$, and $\lambda_{\rm next}$.

If all $N$ attempts are rejected, return rejection-budget-exhausted. The equality in the boundary test is exact for exact arithmetic and is the equality test on stored values in a computed run. No claim is made that every finite budget succeeds.

## Definition

Inputs are a transcription record from [[alg-ctrl1-runge-kutta-shooting-and-collocation-transcription]], a primal initial iterate $z_0$ and full multiplier iterate $\mu_0=(
u_0,\lambda_0)$ in the fixed equality/inequality constraint ordering, an optional canonical QP start $(x^0,y^0,s^0)$ with nonnegative primal variables $x^0$, free equality multipliers $y^0$, and nonnegative dual slacks $s^0$, an SQP model builder, and finite nonnegative tolerances $	au_p,	au_d,	au_c,	au_{stage},	au_{quad}$. The stage and quadrature tolerances must match those bound into the transcription record. The KKT tolerances $	au_p,	au_d,	au_c$ bound primal feasibility, stationarity, and multiplier-feasibility/complementarity; in the QP route $	au_c$ also bounds the primal-dual gap. Also supply an SQP update cap $K\ge0$, QP update cap $N\ge0$, positive penalty/backtracking caps $R,J_{max}\ge1$, merit parameters $ho_0>0$, $\gamma>1$, $0< eta,\sigma<1$, and the finite-budget exact-Hessian branch selector and identified active set when that branch is requested. The IVP estimator uses its own declared controller tolerances; its status is not treated as an error certificate.

The SQP model builder is a deterministic finite procedure which, at each queried full state $(z_k,
u_k,\lambda_k)$, returns either a failure status or the finite NLP data $f_k,h_k,g_k,Dh_k,Dg_k$, its objective gradient, a symmetric positive-definite SQP model matrix $W_k$ when the merit branch is selected, and the exact Lagrangian Hessian when the exact-Hessian branch is selected. The model matrix may depend on the supplied current multiplier vectors. For the exact-Hessian branch with identified active set $I$, evaluate that Hessian with equality multipliers $
u_k$, active inequality multipliers $(\lambda_k)_I$, and zero inactive multipliers; its required positivity is the separate reduced-curvature condition of the exact step, not full positive definiteness. It must use $g_i\le0$ and nonnegative inequality multipliers. In the merit branch, the associated quadratic subproblem is exactly $\min_p 
abla f_k^Tp+	frac12p^TW_kp$ subject to $h_k+Dh_kp=0$ and $g_k+Dg_kp\le0$. For that branch, the builder also supplies the active equality/inequality row data required by [[alg-sqp-merit-globalization-with-finite-budgets]]. Solver tolerances are used as follows: $	au_p$ bounds the norm of equality and positive inequality violations, $	au_d$ bounds the stationarity residual, and $	au_c$ bounds multiplier-feasibility and complementarity residuals. The stage and quadrature tolerances are passed to the transcription's corresponding residual and certified-error checks. The IVP estimator uses its own declared controller tolerances and has a separate status; its embedded difference is not a certified error bound. Any called builder, evaluator, canonicalizer, or solver returns a value or failure status in finite time.

First audit the transcription dimensions, sampled domains, and data status fields. If stage construction failed, return the partial record with its stage and NLP statuses and do not call a solver. If the model satisfies [[lem-ctrl1-lqr-transcription-is-a-convex-quadratic-program]], map its finite quadratic objective and affine constraints to canonical LP/QP form: replace each free variable $z_i$ by $z_i^+-z_i^-$ with $z_i^+,z_i^-\ge0$; for each affine inequality $a_i^Tz+d_i\le0$, add a primal slack $\xi_i\ge0$ and equality $a_i^Tz+\xi_i=-d_i$; retain existing equalities; and transform the quadratic objective by substitution. The transcription record supplies finite stored coefficient arrays. Canonicalize using exact rational arithmetic on their dyadic values, then round each resulting coefficient once to the nearest normal representable value under [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], preserving exact zeros; any range failure makes the QP route inapplicable. Check the resulting equality matrix by exact rational row elimination; if it is rank deficient or the conversion is otherwise inadmissible, mark the QP route inapplicable and proceed to SQP. The optional start $(x^0,y^0,s^0)$ is in these converted coordinates and is checked constructively: require every primal coordinate, including each added $\xi_i$, and every dual slack coordinate $s^0$ to be strictly positive, and require $y^0$ to be finite with the correct equality dimension. If it is absent or fails this check, record `strict-start-unavailable` and proceed to SQP; do not infer infeasibility or decide whether some other strict start exists. If it passes, call [[alg-primal-dual-newton-residual-method-for-lp-qps-and-symmetric-cones]] once with centering and fraction-to-boundary parameters both $1/2$, $\epsilon_p=	au_p$, $\epsilon_d=\min(	au_d,	au_c)$, $\epsilon_g=	au_c$, and cap $N$. The minimum in $\epsilon_d$ ensures the supplier's single tolerance for both its dual and complementarity residuals meets each requested bound; $\epsilon_g$ separately bounds the certified primal-dual gap. If it returns `invalid-input` or `strict-start-unavailable`, record that QP status and proceed to SQP. Return every other status and audited residuals. `certified-gap` certifies the resulting stored canonical floating-point QP, interpreted as exact dyadic rationals, under [[thm-fraction-to-boundary-and-primal-dual-gap-certificates]]; it is not a certificate for the unsampled continuous problem. A `residual-candidate` remains a candidate. No other QP status is reinterpreted as success.

If the QP route is inapplicable or lacks a supplied strict start, run the SQP branch only when the transcription status is solver-ready `constructed`; otherwise return its `not-smooth-nlp` or model-construction status without an SQP call. Initialize $(z,
u,\lambda)=(z_0,
u_0,\lambda_0)$ and verify the full multiplier dimensions. An invalid state returns `model-build-failure` with its last available record. For $k=0,1,\ldots,K$, in order, query the model builder at the entire current state $(z_k,
u_k,\lambda_k)$, propagating any builder failure without changing that state, and compute
$$r_p=(h_k,[g_k]_+),\quad r_d=
abla f_k+Dh_k^T
u_k+Dg_k^T\lambda_k,\quad r_\lambda=[-\lambda_k]_+,\quad r_c=(\lambda_{k,i}g_{k,i})_i,$$
where positive parts are componentwise. If $\|r_p\|\le	au_p$, $\|r_d\|\le	au_d$, $\|r_\lambda\|\le	au_c$, and $\|r_c\|\le	au_c$, return `kkt-residual-met` with the current decision and residual record; this is an approximate KKT candidate unless all residuals are exactly zero. If $k=K$, return `budget-exhausted`. Otherwise, if the exact-Hessian branch is selected and an active set $I$ has been correctly identified, call [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]] at the current pair $(z_k,(
u_k,(\lambda_k)_I))$ with inactive multipliers set to zero, using the exact Hessian evaluated at that same pair. On its successful full Newton-pair return $(z^+,\mu^+)$, use $z^+$, place the equality and active-inequality components of $\mu^+$ into the full vectors $(
u,\lambda)$, and set inactive inequality components to zero; any failure stops with that status without changing the current state. u^{QP},\lambda^{QP})$ to set $(z,
u,\lambda)=(z^+,
u^{QP},\lambda^{QP})$ for the next model-builder query. Retain the complete supplier record, including its retained equality basis and selected inequality support. Every return is a result record with the last available decision variables, the full current SQP multiplier vectors when that branch has been reached, its last supplier record when one exists, defect residuals, path/endpoint constraint residuals, KKT residuals, objective value, and separate `nlp_status`, `implicit_stage_status`, `ivp_status`, `quadrature_status`, `mesh_status`, and `budget_status` fields. ## Statement

Fix a mesh and a finite transcription generated from the pointwise smooth data in [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]]. Suppose its NLP functions have continuous derivatives through order three on an open neighborhood of a KKT point $(z_*,\mu_*)$, LICQ holds there, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and the second-order sufficient condition holds on the critical cone. Then, after the correct active set is identified, the exact-Hessian full-step branch using [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]] is well-defined from a sufficiently close primal-dual start and converges quadratically to $(z_*,\mu_*)$. The finite-budget dispatch of [[alg-ctrl1-finite-budget-transcription-solver-dispatch]] may terminate before this local convergence is realized.

This also has the following conditional mesh-family conclusion. For each mesh index $N$, let $\mathcal K_N:Z_N\to Y_N$ be the square active-set KKT residual map of a finite transcription, with finite-dimensional normed spaces $Z_N,Y_N$, and let $z_N^0\in Z_N$ be a reference primal-dual pair. Let $Z$ be a common Banach space containing the continuous primal and multiplier fields, with bounded linear reconstruction maps $E_N:Z_N\to Z$ that use the same fixed norms and satisfy $\sup_N\|E_N\|\le C_E$. Suppose a continuous KKT pair $z^\dagger\in Z$ and mesh-consistent constraints satisfy $\|E_Nz_N^0-z^\dagger\|_Z\to0$ and $\|\mathcal K_N(z_N^0)\|_{Y_N}\le\varepsilon_N\to0$. Suppose the discrete sensitivity maps $D\mathcal K_N(z_N^0):Z_N\to Y_N$ are invertible with $\|D\mathcal K_N(z_N^0)^{-1}\|\le\beta$ uniformly, and $D\mathcal K_N$ is $L$-Lipschitz on a common radius $r$ about each $z_N^0$, with constants independent of $N$. For all sufficiently large $N$, require $2\beta\varepsilon_N\le r$ and $2\beta^2L\varepsilon_N\le\frac12$. Then there is a unique active-set KKT root $z_N^*$ in the radius-$2\beta\varepsilon_N$ ball, and $\|E_Nz_N^*-z^\dagger\|_Z\le\|E_Nz_N^0-z^\dagger\|_Z+2C_E\beta\varepsilon_N\to0$. If these roots satisfy LICQ, strict complementarity, SOSC, and a common local full-step basin for exact-Hessian SQP, then the exact-Hessian iterates from starts in that basin converge quadratically to $z_N^*$ for each such mesh. The varying systems are compared through the reconstruction maps and their fixed norms; this conclusion makes no global optimizer, path-feasibility, or finite-budget convergence claim.
